# Cognitive Agency\chaptersubtitle{The Five Stages of Physical AI} {#sec-cognition}

![**Systems Organ Focus: The End-to-End Cognitive Lifecycle.** Tracing the closed-loop dataflow across the five sensory-motor stages: Spatial Perception, Temporal Memory, Semantic Deliberation, Trajectory Planning, and Real-Time Safety Execution ($W_t \to O_t \to S_t \to I_t \to \tau_t \to u_t \to W_{t+1}$).](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch03 fig-pos="H" width=100%}

*How does an embodied system transform raw, noisy sensory fluxes from an unyielding physical world into safe, purposeful, and kinodynamically feasible physical actions?*

In classical computing, software is decoupled from physical time: if an algorithm stalls behind glass, nothing breaks. In Physical AI, time is an unyielding dynamical coordinate. While a neural model deliberates in silicon, inertia carries moving linkages forward, gravity accelerates ungrounded masses, and sensory observations decay toward obsolescence. If the computational pipeline fails to deliver valid actuation commands before physical reality diverges from internal belief, the result is mechanical collision. To survive in dynamic physical environments, embodied intelligence must be structured into five fundamental cognitive stages that transform raw sensory fluxes into safe, purposeful physical actions.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.callout-objective}
After studying this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Deconstruct Embodied Agency:** Map physical tasks across the five canonical cognitive stages: Spatial Perception, Temporal Memory, Semantic Reasoning, Trajectory Planning, and Safety Execution.
2. **Trace the Cognitive Lifecycle:** Follow the closed-loop causal dataflow from environmental state through sensory transduction, latent memory, intent generation, trajectory synthesis, motor execution, and physical state mutation ($W_t \to O_t \to S_t \to I_t \to \tau_t \to u_t \to W_{t+1}$).
3. **Contrast Classical and Modern Paradigms:** Trace the evolutionary leap from handcrafted classical algorithms (SIFT, EKFs, PDDL, RRT*, PID) to modern Physical AI foundation models (ViTs, JEPAs, VLAs, Diffusion Policies, CBF-QPs).
4. **Analyze the Scale vs. Latency Dilemma:** Explain why monolithic end-to-end neural controllers fail on physical hardware and why multi-rate layered intelligence is mandatory.
5. **Differentiate Observation from State:** Model how dynamic world models and kinematic frame trees maintain spatial belief across sensory occlusions and dropouts ($O_t \neq S_t$).
6. **Formulate Bounded Intent:** Structure high-level semantic directives into verifiable physical goals without granting unmitigated electrical authority to stochastic models.
7. **Ground Agency Across High-Stakes Domains:** Analyze the manifestation of the five cognitive stages across terrestrial mobility, precision surgery, robotic manipulation, and cybernetic energy grids.

**Core Chapter Takeaway:** Embodied physical intelligence is not a single end-to-end neural network; it is a five-stage cognitive lifecycle that transforms raw sensory fluxes into metric state beliefs, bounded intent, and kinodynamically safe physical actions.
:::

## The Cognitive Imperative: Why Embodiment Demands Layered Intelligence

Modern computer science is divided by an ideological and architectural schism between disembodied software intelligence and classical physical control (@fig-locator-ch03). In the software and machine learning community, intelligence is treated as an unconstrained statistical optimization problem formulated in high-level frameworks like PyTorch and evaluated on static offline benchmarks or synchronous simulators [@vaswani2017attention; @brohan2023rt2]. In this digital regime, computation is fundamentally decoupled from physical duration. An episodic simulation loop halts the universe while matrix multiplications execute across GPU clusters, and a web service absorbs hundred-millisecond inference stalls by buffering requests behind network sockets. Success is measured by loss curves, token throughput, and parameter scale.

In contrast, classical robotics and embedded control treat intelligence through the lens of continuous Newtonian dynamics, deterministic state machines, and hard real-time execution [@brooks1986robust; @kopetz2011real]. To an embedded engineer or control theorist, correctness is fundamentally a function of both logical precision and exact temporal predictability: an answer delivered five milliseconds late is not merely degraded, but physically catastrophic. Because physical actuators break when subjected to software faults, the classical robotics discipline has historically rejected high-capacity neural networks as opaque, non-deterministic hazards that cannot be trusted near safety-critical hardware.

Physical AI resolves this historical division not by compromising on model capacity or physical safety, but by establishing a rigorous systems architecture that mediates between them (@fig-great-tension). Rather than discarding the expressive power of modern foundation models or abandoning the hard mathematical guarantees of classical control theory, Physical AI re-architects their relationship. It treats high-capacity learned models not as monolithic end-to-end controllers, but as untrusted proposal generators bounded by strict hardware isolation boundaries, formal real-time contracts, and deterministic safety enforcers [@leveson2011engineering]. In doing so, Physical AI creates an architectural framework where open-world semantic comprehension and microsecond-level kinematic safety coexist on the same embodied platform.

![**The Core Architectural Tension in Physical AI.** Reconciling the open-world reasoning capacity and variable compute latency of foundation models on application processors (MPU/GPU) with the microsecond determinism and unyielding dynamics of physical hardware on dedicated microcontrollers (MCU).](figures/fig03_great_tension.svg){#fig-great-tension width=100%}

To build a dependable embodied system, three distinct engineering disciplines must be reconciled:

* **Maya (CS/ML):** Seeks to harness high-capacity representations—Vision Transformers, multimodal vision-language models, and generative diffusion policies—to give physical machines open-world generalization, semantic commonsense, and zero-shot task adaptability.
* **Carlos (ECE/Embedded):** Enforces the physical constraints of silicon and electronic buses—bounding Direct Memory Access (DMA) channel contention, eliminating non-deterministic operating system scheduling jitter, synchronizing hardware clock domains, and executing safety loops in zero-allocation static SRAM (`malloc = 0`).
* **Alex (MechE/Robotics):** Grounds every commanded motion in Newtonian mechanics—respecting momentum conservation ($p = mv$), enforcing dynamic braking distances, protecting harmonic drive gear teeth from destructive jerk shock ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}}$), and verifying forward invariance against geometric obstacle boundaries.

The central tension in modern embodied systems arises from the divergent scaling laws of artificial intelligence and physical dynamics. Contemporary machine learning derives its most profound capabilities from extreme computational scale. Autoregressive transformers, multimodal vision-language models, and large-scale diffusion backbones achieve open-world generalizability precisely because they execute hundreds of billions of floating-point operations across massive parameter spaces. However, this semantic competence comes at the expense of computational duration and execution determinism. A forward pass through an 8-billion parameter foundation model requires tens to hundreds of milliseconds on high-end neural accelerators. Furthermore, latency distributions exhibit long $P_{99}$ tails caused by variable token sequence lengths during autoregressive decoding, Unified Memory Architecture (UMA) bus contention, operating system kernel scheduling jitter, and hardware Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) under thermal load.

In the physical world, computational latency directly consumes physical safety margin because inertia, gravity, and kinetic momentum never pause for silicon. A physical body in motion obeys continuous dynamical laws: while algorithms compute in silicon, moving mass continues coasting under momentum, and the external world continuously evolves ($W_t \to W_{t+1}$).

Monolithic software architectures fail in embodied systems because coupling high-level deliberation directly to physical actuation pollutes deterministic control loops with stochastic computational latency jitter. When roboticists attempt to deploy end-to-end neural policies that map raw sensory pixels directly to motor torques in a single synchronous loop in software, the entire system becomes hostage to the weakest link in the computational chain. If a vision-language model takes $800\text{ ms}$ to interpret an unexpected obstacle, or if a language runtime triggers a garbage collection pause, the actuator control loop is starved of reference updates. The physical motors either hold obsolete torque setpoints, oscillate uncontrollably due to phase lag, or trip hardware over-current protections. Monolithic execution creates an unresolvable trade-off: forcing the model to run at real-time control frequencies (such as $500\text{ Hz}$) artificially constrains its parameter size and reasoning depth, while allowing the model to run at its natural deliberative frequency (such as $1\text{ Hz}$) leaves the physical machine unguided and unstable during the multi-hundred-millisecond deliberation window.

To reconcile high-capacity semantic reasoning with deterministic physical stability, embodied intelligence must be decomposed into a multi-rate cognitive hierarchy spanning distinct functional stages. An intelligent agent interacting with the physical world must simultaneously solve problems across radically different temporal horizons. At the slowest scale ($0.5\text{ to } 2\text{ Hz}$), the agent requires deep semantic scene comprehension to interpret open-world directives, reason over spatial affordances, and plan long-horizon tasks. At intermediate scales ($20\text{ to } 50\text{ Hz}$), the agent must synthesize continuous, jerk-bounded kinematic trajectories that amortize computational delays across temporal action chunks. At the fastest scale ($1000\text{ Hz}$), the agent must modulate multi-phase motor currents, evaluate hard real-time safety barriers, and guarantee physical invariance on dedicated real-time silicon.

This multi-rate physical reality dictates a principled functional decomposition of the embodied cognitive pipeline into five foundational stages: spatial perception, temporal memory, semantic reasoning, trajectory planning, and deterministic execution. We begin by formalizing the closed-loop causal lifecycle and its master dataflow equation governing continuous cyber-physical interaction (Section 3.2). We then trace how raw physical fluxes are transduced into geometrically metric 3D affordance tokens during spatial perception (Section 3.3), and how predictive world models sustain persistent spatial beliefs across occlusions and sensor dropouts within temporal memory (Section 3.4). Next, we analyze how high-capacity foundation models synthesize structured, time-bounded intent leases during semantic reasoning (Section 3.5), and how generative action-chunking policies decode these leases into kinodynamically smooth, jerk-bounded motion trajectories (Section 3.6). We explore how bare-metal microcontrollers evaluate Control Barrier Functions at kilohertz rates in zero-allocation static memory to guarantee physical safety invariants during real-time reflex enforcement (Section 3.7). Finally, we demonstrate the cross-archetype universality of this lifecycle across representative high-stakes domains (Section 3.8), stress-test the architectural trade-offs of the five cognitive stages through high-stakes system thought experiments (Section 3.9), and provide the forward systems handoff to the multi-rate execution hierarchy in @sec-hierarchy (Section 3.10).


## Deconstructing Physical Agency: The Closed-Loop Causal Lifecycle

Embodied physical agency is not a monolithic feedforward transfer function, but an endogenous, closed-loop causal lifecycle. Where digital machine learning models process isolated inputs to generate advisory classifications or token sequences behind glass, an embodied agent operates within an unyielding dynamical continuum. Every computational operation executed by the agent is both a consequence of prior physical states and the direct cause of future physical transformations. To govern this continuous interaction without succumbing to computational latency spikes or mechanical instability, physical intelligence is partitioned into five functionally specialized sensory-motor stages: Spatial Perception, Temporal Memory, Semantic Reasoning, Trajectory Planning, and Real-Time Safety Execution.

This end-to-end cognitive lifecycle unfolds along a continuous causal dataflow chain, transforming external physical reality into internal metric representations, high-level intent, kinodynamic motion profiles, and electrical actuator commands:

$$W_t \xrightarrow{\quad\text{Perceive}\quad} O_t \xrightarrow{\quad\text{Remember}\quad} S_t \xrightarrow{\quad\text{Reason}\quad} I_t \xrightarrow{\quad\text{Plan}\quad} \tau_t \xrightarrow{\quad\text{Enforce}\quad} u_t \xrightarrow{\quad\text{Actuate}\quad} W_{t+1}$$

In this formal dataflow, each variable resolves a distinct boundary between the physical environment and the machine's internal computation:

* **$W_t \in \mathcal{W}$ (Physical World State):** The true, unobserved continuous state of the external environment at time $t$, encompassing continuous spatial coordinates, velocities, structural rigidities, friction coefficients, temperature fields, and dynamic obstacles.
* **$O_t \in \mathcal{O}$ (Raw Observation Tensors):** The instantaneous sensory fluxes transducted by physical sensors, represented as structured multi-modal tensors: optical camera frames, LiDAR point clouds, joint encoder angles, and IMU linear accelerations and angular rates.
* **$S_t \in \mathcal{S}$ (State Belief Tuple):** Because instantaneous observations are corrupted by sensor noise, dynamic occlusions, and transport delays, the temporal memory stage fuses $O_t$ into an internal metric state belief $\hat{\mathbf{T}} \in SE(3)$, spatial uncertainty bounds, and compact latent world model embeddings.
* **$I_t = \mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} \in \mathcal{I}$ (Expiring Semantic Intent Lease):** Conditioned on this continuous spatial-temporal belief, the high-level semantic reasoning stage deliberates over operational objectives to synthesize a time-bounded intent lease tuple $\langle \mathcal{G}_{\text{task}}, \mathcal{S}_{\text{hull}}, t_{\text{issue}}, \Delta t_{\text{lease}}, \mathbf{w}_{\text{target}}, \mathcal{B}_{\text{keepout}} \rangle$.
* **$\tau_t \in \mathcal{T}$ (Kinodynamic Motion Trajectory):** The trajectory planning stage translates this bounded intent into a continuous $\mathcal{C}^2$-smooth reference trajectory queue defined over a multi-step lookahead horizon.
* **$u_t \in \mathcal{U}$ (Certified Low-Level Control):** The real-time execution engine filters candidate trajectory waypoints through deterministic Control Barrier Functions to emit instantaneous electrical control signals: pulse-width modulated (PWM) inverter gate duty cycles, three-phase stator current setpoints, or hydraulic valve commands.

These electrical signals energize physical actuators, exerting generalized forces and torques that irreversibly alter the external environment into state $W_{t+1}$ over the fundamental physical control tick $\Delta t_{\text{tick}}$, which in turn generates the subsequent endogenous observation $O_{t+1}$ and closes the physical feedback loop.

::: {.callout-note title="Concrete Systems Walkthrough: Tracing a Grasp Across the Five Stages"}
To build concrete intuition for how the master dataflow equation functions in hardware, trace a single cognitive cycle for a robotic manipulator picking a delicate glass pharmaceutical vial:

1. **$W_t$ (World):** A glass vial rests on a stainless-steel tray within the robot's physical workspace.
2. **$O_t$ (Perceive):** An RGB-D camera captures an optical frame, while optical joint encoders report instantaneous joint angles.
3. **$S_t$ (Remember):** The state estimator unprojects 2D pixels to $SE(3)$ coordinates using calibrated camera geometry, fusing point clouds with forward kinematics to register the vial's 3D pose and track spatial uncertainty.
4. **$I_t$ (Reason):** A high-level Vision-Language-Action model deliberates over the scene and emits an Expiring Intent Lease $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$: targeting a safe pre-grasp waypoint above the vial neck, valid for a bounded duration of $500\text{ ms}$ within a certified workspace volume.
5. **$\tau_t$ (Plan):** A $50\text{ Hz}$ trajectory planner decodes this intent lease into a smooth, 16-step $\mathcal{C}^2$-continuous spline that respects joint velocity and acceleration limits.
6. **$u_t$ (Enforce):** A $1000\text{ Hz}$ bare-metal microcontroller evaluates a real-time safety barrier guarding against table collisions, certifies the candidate motion, and commands stator phase currents to the motor drives.
7. **$W_{t+1}$ (Actuate):** Motor phase currents build electromagnetic torque across stator coils, accelerating the robot's linkages, displacing the gripper closer to the vial, and altering the physical world state to $W_{t+1}$.
:::

![The Complete End-to-End Physical Agent Lifecycle. Tracing the closed-loop causal dataflow across the five canonical sensory-motor stages: Spatial Perception ($W_t \to O_t$), Temporal Memory ($O_t \to S_t$), Semantic Deliberation ($S_t \to I_t$), Trajectory Synthesis ($I_t \to \tau_t$), and Real-Time Safety Execution ($\tau_t \to u_t \to W_{t+1}$). As illustrated in @fig-agent-workflow, each of these five canonical stages resolves a distinct physical or representational boundary between the continuous, unyielding physical universe and the discrete, computational silicon substrate. We now formally examine each stage, analyzing its mathematical formulation, its historical evolution from classical robotics to modern Physical AI foundation models, and its specific systems role in the embodied cognitive lifecycle.

## Stage 1: Spatial Perception and Metric Grounding

Spatial perception resolves the *Transduction and Projection Boundary*, converting uncalibrated physical energy fluxes into geometrically metric, spatially grounded 3D representations. 

To build an intuitive physical mental model of perception, consider what an optical camera actually sees. A camera image is a flat, 2D shadow of a three-dimensional world: infinite physical points along a single line-of-sight ray collapse onto the exact same pixel coordinate $(u, v)$. A small $10\text{ cm}$ hand tool held $0.5\text{ m}$ in front of the lens subtends the identical angular pixel size as a massive $2\text{ m}$ steel beam $10\text{ m}$ away. Driving physical robot motors directly from 2D pixel centroids or bounding box detections is fatal because pixel coordinates contain zero physical depth, spatial orientation, or metric scale.

At the silicon hardware level, the physical world manifests as continuous electromagnetic radiation striking silicon photodiode arrays. Collecting enough photons to form an image requires 8 to 15 milliseconds of physical exposure time ($t_{\text{transduce}}$). Once the charge wells are integrated, analog-to-digital converters serialize the voltages into raw byte arrays, which are streamed across Direct Memory Access (DMA) channels into processor memory.

To transform these ungrounded sensory streams into actionable physical knowledge, the three disciplines contribute distinct layers:

* **Maya (CS/ML):** Leverages Vision Transformers (ViTs) and self-supervised backbones (such as DINOv2) to divide images into pixel patches, projecting them into high-dimensional embedding spaces where self-attention extracts dense semantic feature fields and object affordances invariant to lighting and texture changes.
* **Carlos (ECE/Embedded):** Provisions zero-copy coherent DMA ring buffers (`dma_alloc_coherent`) to ingest high-bandwidth camera streams directly into unified memory, tagging each frame with an IEEE 1588 PTP hardware timestamp at the exact midpoint of optical exposure.
* **Alex (MechE/Robotics):** Applies projective geometry and Lie group transformations ($SE(3)$) to unproject 2D pixel rays into 3D metric coordinates and rigidly transform them into the physical robot base frame.

To map a 2D pixel coordinate $(u, v)$ with measured metric depth $d(u, v)$ into a true 3D coordinate $\mathbf{p}_{\text{world}} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ in the robot base frame, the perception engine executes the unified inverse pinhole and rigid-body coordinate transformation:

$$\begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{p}_{\text{world}} \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{T}_{\text{world}\leftarrow\text{cam}} \begin{bmatrix} d(u, v) \cdot \mathbf{K}^{-1} \begin{bmatrix} u \\ v \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

In this fundamental governing relation:

* $(u, v)$ is the 2D discrete pixel coordinate on the sensor grid.
* $\mathbf{K} \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ is the intrinsic camera calibration matrix, containing focal lengths and optical center offsets determined by lens geometry and sensor pixel pitch.
* $d(u, v) \in \mathbb{R}^+$ is the true metric depth along the optical axis measured by active time-of-flight, structured light, or stereo disparity.
* $\mathbf{T}_{\text{world}\leftarrow\text{cam}} \in SE(3)$ is the rigid-body extrinsic transformation matrix, capturing camera orientation ($\mathrm{SO}(3)$) and position relative to the robot's physical base origin.

Only after this geometric unprojection can downstream planning reason about physical reachability, obstacles, and collision boundaries.

In classical robotics, spatial perception relied upon handcrafted, deterministic feature extractors such as SIFT, SURF, and Harris corner detectors combined with geometric epipolar constraints and multi-view bundle adjustment [@hartley2003multiple]. While these classical pipelines provided mathematically rigorous metric guarantees, they were notoriously brittle, failing catastrophically under specular reflections, textureless surfaces, dynamic shadows, and atmospheric obscurants. Modern Physical AI transforms perception through large-scale Vision Transformers (ViTs) and self-supervised visual foundation models such as DINOv2 [@dosovitskiy2020image; @oquab2023dinov2]. Rather than tracking isolated, brittle geometric primitives, modern perception backbones extract dense semantic feature fields and spatial affordance tokens directly from high-dimensional sensor arrays. These learned representations capture rich semantic scene context invariant to lighting and texture changes; when fused with calibrated depth sensors or geometric spatial priors, they reliably ground these rich semantics into metric $SE(3)$ coordinates.

Despite the expressive power of modern perception networks, an instantaneous observation $O_t$ can never serve as a direct command for physical actuation. An observation is fundamentally instantaneous, incomplete, and subject to sensor latency, motion blur, and line-of-sight occlusions. A camera frame reveals only the exposed surfaces of physical objects at the moment of photodiode charge integration ($t_{\text{transduce}}$); it cannot reveal the hidden mass distribution of an occluded object, its continuous velocity vectors (which require temporal finite differences or optical flow gradients across multiple observations), or its future trajectory. To convert instantaneous, fragmented perceptions into dependable operational knowledge, the cognitive pipeline must pass raw spatial representations into persistent temporal memory, establishing the foundation for state estimation analyzed in @sec-perception.

::: {.callout-fallacy title="The 2D Camera Pixel as Metric Ground Truth"}
* **The Common Assumption:** Modern visual foundation models (such as ViTs, CLIP, and DINOv2) can detect, segment, and track objects with high semantic accuracy directly within the pixel array $\mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}$. Therefore, an embodied policy can bypass explicit geometric calibration and directly drive joint actuators toward 2D pixel centroids or optical bounding boxes.
* **The Physical Reality:** A 2D camera image represents a lossy projective ray collapse ($SE(3) \to \mathbb{R}^2$); ungrounded pixel coordinates contain zero metric depth, spatial orientation, or physical scale. Furthermore, optical sensors suffer rolling-shutter spatial shearing under ego-motion, lens distortion, and line-of-sight occlusions. A policy commanding joint torques directly from 2D pixel coordinates cannot distinguish between a $10\text{ cm}$ tool at $0.5\text{ m}$ distance and a $2\text{ m}$ structural hazard at $10\text{ m}$ distance, inevitably triggering kinematic singularities, unmodeled collisions, or joint limit overruns.
* **The Systems Invariant:** Raw sensory fluxes must be lifted into calibrated metric reference frames ($SE(3)$) via verified camera extrinsics and geometric depth fusion before entering downstream cognitive stages ($O_t \subset SE(3)$). Never command physical actuation directly from ungrounded 2D pixel space.
:::

## Stage 2: Temporal Memory and World Modeling

Temporal memory resolves the *Epistemic and Partial Observability Boundary*, bridging the critical divergence between what an agent instantaneously observes and the true physical state of the operating environment ($O_t \neq S_t$). 

To build an intuitive physical mental model of temporal memory, consider navigating your own living room after the lights suddenly go out. You do not instantly forget where the walls, couch, or doorways are located; your brain maintains an internal spatial map of the room that persists even when your eyes receive zero photons. If a family member steps across the room and momentarily occludes a chair, you do not assume the chair has ceased to exist. However, as you take multiple steps in the dark without fresh visual feedback, your internal positional uncertainty grows until you must slow down to avoid stubbing your toe.

In embodied systems, complete observability is a physical impossibility. Dynamic obstacles pass behind structural pillars, camera lenses suffer momentary optical flare, LiDAR beams reflect away from specular metallic surfaces, and communication buses incur scheduling transport delays. If an intelligent agent relied exclusively on its instantaneous sensory observation $O_t$, an obstacle would vanish from existence the instant it slipped behind an occlusion, causing the machine to steer directly into it during subsequent maneuvers.

Furthermore, temporal memory acts as an essential physical buffer against computational deliberation latency ($\Delta t$). Because deep neural deliberation and trajectory optimization require non-zero execution time, the physical universe continues moving while algorithms compute. If an autonomous robot designs a motion plan conditioned on an unprojected observation captured at historical instant $t_{\text{capture}}$, by the time the plan arrives at the actuators at $t_{\text{deploy}} = t_{\text{capture}} + \Delta t$, the machine has physically traveled forward under momentum. Deploying an action computed for an obsolete pose induces severe trajectory tracking errors, phase-lag oscillations, or structural collisions.

To reconcile these physical challenges, the three disciplines coordinate across temporal memory:

* **Maya (CS/ML):** Develops Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and Recurrent State-Space Models (RSSMs) that map raw observations into compact latent feature vectors $\mathbf{z} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, predicting how latent physical affordances evolve under candidate actions without wasting compute decoding millions of task-irrelevant background pixels.
* **Carlos (ECE/Embedded):** Rejects naive multi-frame token concatenation—which triggers quadratic compute growth $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ and exhausts memory bandwidth with massive Key-Value (KV) cache traffic—and instead enforces fixed-size ring buffers in deterministic memory that execute recursive state updates in strictly bounded $\mathcal{O}(1)$ time.
* **Alex (MechE/Robotics):** Anchors learned latent states to Lie-algebraic kinematic frame trees and integrates continuous rigid-body dynamics $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u})$ forward across the computational delay $\Delta t$, guaranteeing that planned footholds or grasping waypoints align with the robot's future physical pose.

To project the machine's estimated metric state forward across the computational deliberation horizon $\Delta t$, the temporal memory stage evaluates the continuous dynamic state projection:

$$\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t+\Delta t} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_t + \int_{t}^{t+\Delta t} \mathbf{f}(\hat{\mathbf{x}}(\tau), \mathbf{u}(\tau))\, d\tau$$

In this dynamic projection model, $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_t$ represents the estimated metric state vector at the observation timestamp (encompassing 3D position, linear velocity, orientation quaternion, and angular velocity), $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u})$ represents the continuous rigid-body equations of motion governing the platform, and $\Delta t$ is the forward computational deliberation horizon. 

To understand how forward state projection neutralizes latency in practice, consider an autonomous quadruped robot trotting at forward velocity $v_x = 2.0\text{ m/s}$. The robot's stereo vision pipeline operates at $20\text{ Hz}$ ($50\text{ ms}$ frame period), while high-level semantic deliberation requires $\Delta t = 80\text{ ms}$ inference latency on an embedded neural accelerator. If the downstream planner designs foot placement using the unprojected visual state from $t = 0\text{ ms}$, the robot physically travels $v_x \cdot \Delta t = 2.0\text{ m/s} \times 0.080\text{ s} = 0.160\text{ m}$ ($16.0\text{ cm}$) before the first trajectory waypoint is dispatched. A $16.0\text{ cm}$ foot placement error on uneven terrain is sufficient to trip the quadruped and cause dynamic roll-over. By integrating forward kinematics across the delay, the temporal memory stage projects the platform pose forward to where the quadruped *will* be upon action deployment.

Historically, classical robotics managed partial observability through Extended Kalman Filters (EKFs), Unscented Kalman Filters, and non-linear factor graph optimizers [@kalman1960new; @thrun2005probabilistic; @barfoot2017state]. These algorithms maintained explicit Gaussian belief distributions over kinematic poses and velocities, integrating rigid kinematic frame trees through continuous geometric updates. However, these classical techniques hit an unyielding wall regarding partial observability failure: they required meticulously hand-engineered transition models and struggled to maintain object permanence for complex, non-rigid entities that underwent prolonged visual occlusions. 

Modern Physical AI augments these metric kinematic trees with deep predictive world models and Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) [@lecun2022path; @assran2023self; @hafner2023mastering]. Instead of falling into the computational trap of predicting raw, high-frequency pixel sequences—which wastes capacity modeling task-irrelevant noise like dynamic shadows or textures—modern latent world models encode observations into compact, geometrically structured latent embeddings that capture task-relevant dynamics, object permanency, and physical affordances. These learned embeddings do not blindly replace classical metric state, but rather wrap around it, grounding abstract semantic predictions back into the metric kinematic tree.

This synthesis of metric kinematic trees and predictive latent representations forms the dynamic core examined in @sec-state, providing the stable physical foundation necessary for the high-level semantic reasoning stage that follows.

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Context Windows Substitute for Latent World Models"}
* **The Common Assumption:** Modern multimodal transformers feature massive context windows capable of processing millions of tokens. Rather than maintaining explicit state estimators, kinematic frame trees, or dynamic world models, an embodied system can simply concatenate raw historical sensor tokens $[O_{t-k}, \dots, O_t]$ into the model prompt and rely on self-attention to maintain temporal state and object permanence.
* **The Physical Reality:** Transformer self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ in compute and $\mathcal{O}(N)$ in KV-cache DRAM memory traffic. Concatenating high-bandwidth visual tokens inflates inference latency from tens of milliseconds to multiple seconds, breaching the physical Freshness Wall ($\Delta t \gg \Delta t_{\text{wall}}$). More critically, self-attention across token histories cannot enforce rigid-body kinematic transformations ($SE(3)$), momentum conservation, or numerical velocity integration; when visual occlusions occur, attention weights drift, hallucinating object positions or dropping occluded entities.
* **The Systems Invariant:** Epistemic state belief ($S_t$) must be maintained through recursive state estimation, Lie-algebraic kinematic frame trees, and compact latent world models operating with bounded $\mathcal{O}(1)$ temporal memory overhead. Historical token accumulation is not a substitute for dynamical state estimation.
:::

## Stage 3: Semantic Reasoning and Intent Generation

Semantic reasoning resolves the *Grounding and Deliberation Boundary*, translating open-world, high-level task specifications into verifiable, time-bounded physical objectives. 

To build an intuitive physical mental model of semantic reasoning, consider an architect issuing a signed, time-limited work permit or lease for an active construction zone. The permit specifies the high-level task (e.g., "excavate foundation trench"), defines the exact spatial boundaries within which machinery may operate, and sets strict keepout zones around buried electrical cables. Crucially, the permit contains an unforgeable hardware timestamp and a strict expiration countdown (e.g., valid for 30 minutes). If the operator fails to renew the permit before the countdown reaches zero, all heavy equipment is automatically locked in a safe state. The architect does not grab the hydraulic levers and steer the bulldozer; they establish the authorized operating envelope within which autonomous machinery may work.

In embodied intelligence, the highest tier of cognition requires understanding natural language instructions, evaluating complex multi-step causal dependencies, reasoning over physical affordances, and dynamically re-planning when unexpected environmental anomalies occur. Operating at a deliberative cadence of $0.5\text{ to }2\text{ Hz}$, this stage interprets the current spatial-temporal state belief $S_t$ to determine *what* physical outcome the agent should pursue over the upcoming task horizon.

To bridge semantic flexibility with physical safety, the three disciplines divide responsibilities:

* **Maya (CS/ML):** Deploys large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) backbones trained on massive multimodal datasets [@driess2023palme; @brohan2023rt2; @kim2024openvla], leveraging their semantic commonsense to decompose ambiguous natural language directives (e.g., "safely clear the spilled chemical vial") into structured spatial waypoints and affordance tokens.
* **Carlos (ECE/Embedded):** Enforces strict temporal isolation by treating the foundation model as an untrusted proposal generator, running lease expiration watchdogs on hardware timers with monotonic clock timestamps to guarantee that a stalled GPU forward pass never causes unguided actuator runaway.
* **Alex (MechE/Robotics):** Defines certified convex workspace hulls ($\mathcal{S}_{\text{hull}}$) and keepout hazard volumes ($\mathcal{B}_{\text{keepout}}$), verifying that proposed spatial waypoints remain far from kinematic singularities and collision boundaries before granting execution authority.

Because multi-billion parameter autoregressive models exhibit stochastic inference latencies and non-zero hallucination rates, granting them direct, unmitigated electrical authority over physical motor drives violates fundamental safety engineering principles. Physical AI resolves this vulnerability by restricting the semantic reasoning stage to emitting a formal *Expiring Intent Lease* ($I_t = \mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) [@gray1989leases]:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} = \langle \mathcal{G}_{\text{task}},\, \mathcal{S}_{\text{hull}},\, t_{\text{issue}},\, \Delta t_{\text{lease}},\, \mathbf{w}_{\text{target}},\, \mathcal{B}_{\text{keepout}} \rangle$$

In this formal intent lease structure:

* $\mathcal{G}_{\text{task}}$ is the high-level semantic task descriptor or symbolic goal predicate (e.g., `grasp_chemical_vial`).
* $\mathcal{S}_{\text{hull}} \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathrm{SO}(3)$ is the certified spatial operating hull—a bounded volume in workspace coordinates outside of which physical motion is strictly prohibited.
* $t_{\text{issue}} \in \mathbb{R}^+$ is the synchronized timestamp from the monotonic master hardware clock at the exact moment the lease was signed.
* $\Delta t_{\text{lease}} \in \mathbb{R}^+$ is the explicit validity duration of the lease (typically $0.500\text{ s}$ for a $2\text{ Hz}$ reasoner).
* $\mathbf{w}_{\text{target}}$ is the sequence of discrete 3D metric target waypoints defining the proposed intermediate goal.
* $\mathcal{B}_{\text{keepout}} \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ represents dynamic keepout hazard volumes identified during semantic scene decomposition.

To guarantee that stochastic foundation models can never breach physical safety invariants, downstream real-time microcontrollers continuously evaluate two mandatory contract invariants:

1. **Freshness Invariant:** $t_{\text{now}} - t_{\text{issue}} \le \Delta t_{\text{lease}}$, verifying that the lease has not expired.
2. **Spatial Containment Invariant:** $\mathbf{p}(\tau) \in \mathcal{S}_{\text{hull}} \setminus \mathcal{B}_{\text{keepout}} \quad \forall \tau \in [t_{\text{issue}}, t_{\text{issue}} + \Delta t_{\text{lease}}]$, verifying that all proposed motion remains strictly inside the safe hull and outside all keepout zones.

If the high-level neural reasoner experiences a memory stall or scheduling pause, the active lease expires before the next proposal arrives. Acting as a semantic watchdog, the real-time supervisor detects expiration at microsecond precision and smoothly transitions the platform along a pre-certified stopping path to rest inside $\mathcal{S}_{\text{hull}}$, completely preventing unguided actuator runaway.

When operating nominally, this time-bounded intent lease is handed directly to the trajectory planner to be decoded into physical motion, establishing the architectural privilege separation explored in @sec-intent.

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Softmax Confidence as Execution Safety"}
* **The Common Assumption:** If a multimodal foundation model or Vision-Language-Action policy outputs an action token sequence with high softmax probability ($P(\text{action}) > 0.99$), the proposed action is safe to execute directly on physical actuators without downstream filtering.
* **The Physical Reality:** Softmax confidence measures statistical likelihood under the model's training distribution; it is completely blind to physical invariants, multi-body kinematics, friction cones, thermal limits, and real-time obstacle motion. An out-of-distribution observation or subtle optical illusion can cause an autoregressive model to emit a catastrophic command—such as driving an articulated arm through a concrete wall or commanding extreme over-currents—with near $100\%$ statistical confidence.
* **The Systems Invariant:** Statistical confidence is not physical feasibility. High-level semantic reasoning is an unverified proposal engine; all candidate actions must be filtered through deterministic kinematic solvers and Control Barrier Functions running on isolated real-time silicon.
:::

## Stage 4: Trajectory Planning and Synthesis

Trajectory planning resolves the *Kinodynamic Feasibility Boundary*, converting discrete, high-level semantic intent leases $I_t$ into continuous, collision-free reference trajectories $\tau_t$ that strictly respect the mechanical and physical limits of the hardware. 

To build an intuitive physical mental model of trajectory planning, consider the difference between an Olympic gymnast performing a fluid tumbling pass versus a stop-motion claymation animator posing a puppet frame by frame. An animator can move a puppet to any position between frames with zero physical consequence. But if a physical robot attempts to jump discontinuously between discrete setpoints, or if an algorithm commands sudden steps in acceleration, the result is infinite theoretical jerk ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}} \to \infty$). In physical transmissions, jerk acts as a mechanical hammer: it slams gear teeth together, excites destructive structural resonances, and strips the delicate teeth of cycloidal and harmonic drives. Furthermore, if a robot evaluates single-step neural policies ($H = 1$), any $20\text{ ms}$ compute stall leaves the actuators starved of commands, forcing the machine into a jerky, unstable shudder.

To synthesize fluid, kinodynamically safe motion, the three disciplines unite across trajectory planning:

* **Maya (CS/ML):** Deploys generative Action Chunking Transformers (ACT), Diffusion Policies, and Flow Matching backbones [@chi2023diffusionpolicy; @zhao2023learning; @lipman2022flow] that predict entire multi-step temporal horizons ($H = 16\text{ to }64$ steps), capturing complex multi-modal trajectory distributions (such as smoothly dodging left or right around an obstacle without fatal mode-averaging collisions).
* **Carlos (ECE/Embedded):** Streams these multi-step trajectory chunks across lock-free static SRAM circular queues, buffering the low-level motor drives against GPU inference stalls, memory bus contention, and operating system scheduling jitter.
* **Alex (MechE/Robotics):** Enforces $\mathcal{C}^2$ differential continuity (continuous position, velocity, and acceleration) across trajectory waypoints, strictly bounding mechanical jerk ($|\dddot{\mathbf{q}}| \le j_{\max}$) to protect gearboxes and linkages from torque shock.

To eliminate computational starvation and guarantee differential smoothness, modern Physical AI represents the trajectory output as an action-chunked reference queue:

$$\tau_t = \left\{ \mathbf{q}(t + k\Delta t_{\text{chunk}}),\, \dot{\mathbf{q}}(t + k\Delta t_{\text{chunk}}),\, \ddot{\mathbf{q}}(t + k\Delta t_{\text{chunk}}) \right\}_{k=1}^{H}$$

In this trajectory planning formulation:

* $H \in \mathbb{N}$ is the action chunk lookahead horizon length (typically $H = 16\text{ to }64$ steps).
* $\Delta t_{\text{chunk}} \in \mathbb{R}^+$ is the discrete step size of the trajectory queue (e.g., $20\text{ ms}$, corresponding to a $50\text{ Hz}$ update rate).
* $T_{\text{horizon}} = H \cdot \Delta t_{\text{chunk}}$ is the total temporal preview horizon (e.g., $16 \times 20\text{ ms} = 320\text{ ms}$).
* $\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}}, \ddot{\mathbf{q}}$ are the generalized joint position, velocity, and acceleration vectors.
* Successive overlapping action chunks emitted at timestamps $t_i$ are smoothly blended via exponential receding-horizon temporal ensembling: $\mathbf{a}_{\text{ens}}(t) = \frac{\sum w_i(t) \mathbf{a}_i(t)}{\sum w_i(t)}$ with exponential decay weight $w_i(t) = \exp(-\lambda (t - t_i))$.

With action chunking, the multi-step trajectory queue continuously buffers the joint drives against computational latency jitter: acceleration ramps smoothly along $\mathcal{C}^2$-continuous splines with strictly bounded jerk ($|\dddot{\mathbf{q}}| \le j_{\max} < \infty$), while overlapping chunks are smoothly blended to eliminate boundary discontinuities between inference cycles.

Historically, robotics addressed trajectory synthesis through geometric search and sampling-based algorithms, including Rapidly-exploring Random Trees ($\text{RRT}^*$), Probabilistic Roadmaps (PRM), and numerical non-linear Model Predictive Control (MPC) [@rawlings2017model]. While mathematically rigorous and capable of enforcing explicit obstacle bounds, classical optimization techniques often struggle with high-dimensional contact dynamics, deformable objects, and multi-modal trajectory distributions. For example, when an obstacle blocks a direct path, an agent can pass to the left or to the right; classical mean-squared-error regression averages these two valid modes, commanding a fatal straight-ahead collision. Generative diffusion policies and flow matching resolve this by modeling the full multi-modal distribution, sampling a coherent, collision-free trajectory chunk that is then validated against kinodynamic constraints.

Nevertheless, because generative neural policies remain learned statistical approximations, candidate trajectories are treated as unverified proposals until certified by deterministic real-time hardware, motivating the formal kinodynamic synthesis methods established in @sec-planning.

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Single-Step Planning Under Latency"}
* **The Common Assumption:** Reinforcement learning and Markov Decision Process formulations assume single-step state-action transitions $a_t \sim \pi(s_t)$. An embodied agent should simply evaluate the policy at every tick, emitting a single instantaneous action $a_t$ for immediate execution.
* **The Physical Reality:** Evaluating deep neural policies requires non-zero compute latency $\Delta t_{\text{inference}} \approx 20\text{--}100\text{ ms}$. If an agent dispatches only single-step actions ($H=1$), the physical hardware is starved of commands between inference cycles, forcing the system to hold stale setpoints (zero-order hold) or coast unguided. Furthermore, stitching together discrete single-step predictions without temporal blending creates severe acceleration discontinuities and infinite jerk ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}} \to \infty$), destroying gearboxes and exciting structural vibrations.
* **The Systems Invariant:** Trajectory generation under non-zero compute latency demands temporal Action Chunking ($H \gg 1$) and receding-horizon temporal ensembling ($w_i = \exp(-\lambda(t-t_i))$), generating continuous $\mathcal{C}^2$-smooth trajectory queues that buffer actuators against computational jitter.
:::

## Stage 5: Real-Time Reflex Enforcement

Real-time reflex enforcement resolves the *Silicon-to-Physics Invariant Boundary*, certifying that every electrical signal dispatched to hardware power stages preserves physical safety invariants under hard real-time deadlines. 

To build an intuitive physical mental model of reflex enforcement, consider an active magnetic cushion or virtual forcefield surrounding a physical machine. When the robot operates far inside its safe workspace, the forcefield exerts zero resistance, allowing high-level AI policies full freedom to maneuver. But as the robot approaches a physical obstacle, joint limit, or thermal threshold, the virtual barrier stiffens smoothly and progressively, decelerating the motion to zero before contact can occur. Unlike a physical emergency-stop button or mechanical limit switch—which trips only *after* collision forces have built up—a forward-invariant barrier acts proactively, ensuring the machine never breaches safe physical bounds in the first place.

Operating at the highest system frequency—typically $1000\text{ Hz}$ or faster—on isolated, deterministic microcontroller cores, this stage executes without dynamic memory allocation (`malloc = 0`) to eliminate operating system jitter and priority inversions [@kopetz2011real]. It acts as the ultimate physical gatekeeper, evaluating candidate trajectory waypoints $\tau_t$ against the instantaneous kinematic state of the machine and formal mathematical barrier certificates.

Here, the three disciplines converge on the physical barrier:

* **Maya (CS/ML):** Recognizes that statistical softmax confidence ($P(\text{action}) > 0.99$) is completely blind to physical invariants, multi-body kinematics, friction cones, and thermal limits, happily delegating ultimate execution safety to formal optimization filters.
* **Carlos (ECE/Embedded):** Implements lightweight, deterministic quadratic programming solvers executing in zero-allocation static SRAM (`malloc = 0`) at $1000\text{ Hz}$ with sub-250-microsecond execution budgets, directly driving $20\text{ kHz}$ Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM) gate drivers.
* **Alex (MechE/Robotics):** Formulates Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) that incorporate true multi-body dynamics, joint friction cones, and inductive electrical limits, guaranteeing forward invariance ($\mathcal{C}_{\text{safe}}$) under worst-case hardware operating conditions.

To enforce absolute safety across continuous state spaces, modern Physical AI utilizes Control Barrier Functions formulated as real-time Quadratic Programs (CBF-QPs) [@ames2014control; @ames2019control]. At every 1 kHz control tick, the real-time enforcer solves a convex optimization problem that minimally modifies the proposed high-level acceleration command $\mathbf{u}_{\text{cand}}(\tau_t)$ to guarantee that the machine remains inside the safe operating set:

$$\mathbf{u}_t^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{u} \in \mathcal{U}_{\text{safe}}} \frac{1}{2} \| \mathbf{u} - \mathbf{u}_{\text{cand}}(\tau_t) \|^2 \quad \text{subject to} \quad \dot{h}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u}) + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0$$

In this governing execution formulation:

* $\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is the instantaneous continuous physical state vector (positions, velocities, and contact forces).
* $\mathbf{u} \in \mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ is the certified control actuation command.
* $\mathbf{u}_{\text{cand}}(\tau_t)$ is the candidate unverified reference acceleration or torque proposed by the Stage 4 trajectory planner.
* $h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$ is a scalar barrier function defining safe workspace clearance.
* $\alpha(h)$ is a class $\mathcal{K}$ function that dictates permissible approach speeds—permitting rapid movement when far from danger ($h(\mathbf{x}) \gg 0$) while strictly forcing deceleration to zero as the boundary is approached ($h(\mathbf{x}) \to 0$).

Once certified, the control input $\mathbf{u}_t^*$ is converted into physical motor currents and voltages. Because motor coils have an electrical time constant ($\tau_e = L/R \approx 1\text{--}2\text{ ms}$), real-time execution must operate on dedicated bare-metal microcontrollers at $1000\text{ Hz}$ with $20\text{ kHz}$ PWM switching to match electrical rise times and prevent current spikes or magnetic saturation.

If a proposed trajectory violates kinematic limits, approaches an obstacle, or if upstream compute nodes experience a latency blowout, the real-time enforcer overrides the learned policy instantly. It synthesizes a certified safe control input $\mathbf{u}_t^*$ or executes an emergency stopping trajectory, ensuring that software faults in high-level neural networks never manifest as physical hardware damage. We explore the formal mathematics of barrier functions, real-time architectures, and motor actuation in @sec-enforcement.

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Post-Hoc Limit Switches Substitute for Forward-Invariant Barriers"}
* **The Common Assumption:** Classical PID controllers and joint limit switches have protected industrial machines for decades. As long as the system clamps motor current and trips an emergency stop when a joint limit or tactile bumper switch is contacted, the machine is physically safe.
* **The Physical Reality:** Mechanical limit switches and joint current clamps are reactive (post-hoc); they trigger only *after* a physical collision has occurred or after kinetic energy has built up. In high-speed embodied systems ($v > 1\text{ m/s}$), braking deceleration is physically bounded by friction and torque ($a_{\max}$). If an emergency stop is triggered at the collision boundary ($h=0$), kinetic momentum carries the machine forward by $d = \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\max}}$, crushing the obstacle. Furthermore, joint-level limits are geometrically blind to Cartesian obstacles in workspace coordinates.
* **The Systems Invariant:** Physical safety must be enforced proactively via forward-invariant barrier certificates ($\dot{h}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u}) + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0$) that smoothly decelerate the system *before* the boundary is reached, guaranteeing $\mathcal{C}_{\text{safe}}$ invariance at kilohertz execution rates without relying on reactive post-collision tripping.
:::

## End-to-End Cognitive Lifecycles Across High-Stakes Domains

The five canonical cognitive stages are not theoretical abstractions; they are universal architectural requirements that manifest across every physical embodiment. Regardless of the mechanical medium—whether rolling across planetary regolith, articulating micro-surgical instruments in human tissue, piloting autonomous vehicles through urban intersections, or modulating gigawatts across high-voltage transmission lines—every dependable Physical AI system instantiates these five stages.

@tbl-five-cognitive-stages synthesizes how the five cognitive stages map across representative high-stakes engineering domains, illustrating the structural universality of the embodied sensory-motor lifecycle.

| Cognitive Stage | Planetary Exploration (NASA Mars Rover) | Precision Micro-Surgery (Robotic Laparoscopy) | Urban Autonomous Driving (Level 4 Robotaxi) | Cybernetic Energy Grids (Megawatt Inverters) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage 1: Perceive** | Navcam stereoscopic point clouds, Mastcam multispectral imagery, wheel odometer ticks | Dual stereo endoscope 3D visual feeds, instrument joint encoders, tool-tip force gauges | 64-beam LiDAR point clouds, 8 MP HDR cameras, 1 kHz IMUs, wheel pulse encoders | Rogowski coil AC current waveforms, Hall-effect DC bus sensors, RTD thermal arrays |
| **Stage 2: Remember** | Local digital elevation map (DEM), slip-compensated rover pose tree ($SE(3)$) | 3D deformable organ tissue mesh, dynamic vessel occlusions, kinematic tool frame tree | Multi-sensor dynamic object track history, HD vector lane graph, ego-motion covariance | Sub-cycle AC phase angle ($\Delta\phi$), thermal mass state, virtual synchronous inertia |
| **Stage 3: Reason** | Autonomous science target selection, rock traversability analysis, path waypoint goals | Surgical gesture intent parsing, critical vessel avoidance, step-by-step procedure state | Multi-agent gap acceptance, pedestrian yielding intent, lane-change commitment lease | Grid support mode selection, peak shaving dispatch, fault-ride-through intent lease |
| **Stage 4: Plan** | Minimum-energy kinematic wheel trajectory over rough terrain, rock avoidance splines | Quintic spline tool trajectory, tremor-filtered inverse kinematics, bounded insertion rate | $\mathcal{C}^2$-continuous lane change trajectory, comfort-constrained acceleration profiles | Optimal active/reactive power dispatch curve ($P$-$Q$ droop), harmonic filtering spline |
| **Stage 5: Execute** | Real-time motor current control, rock-bogie differential rocker stall prevention | 1 kHz virtual fixture barrier enforcement, contact force saturation, emergency stop | 1 kHz drive-by-wire steering/braking CBF enforcer, emergency collision avoidance | 20 kHz PWM gate driver switching, inverter over-current lockstep shutdown |

: The Five Cognitive Stages Across High-Stakes Embodied Domains. Mapping the sensory-motor lifecycle across planetary mobility, surgical robotics, autonomous vehicles, and cybernetic energy grids. {#tbl-five-cognitive-stages}

In each domain, the interface between stages is defined by explicit mathematical and temporal contracts:

* **Perception to Memory ($O_t \to S_t$):** Spatial perception delivers timestamped affordance tokens and pose estimates across Direct Memory Access channels, integrating them into global kinematic frame trees using Lie algebra updates.
* **Memory to Reason ($S_t \to I_t$):** Temporal memory continuously filters these observations into persistent, occlusion-free latent world states $S_t$, buffering the deliberative tier against sensor dropouts.
* **Reason to Plan ($I_t \to \tau_t$):** Conditioned on this state belief, the semantic reasoner emits a bounded Expiring Intent Lease ($I_t = \mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$), establishing spatial bounds and validity horizons for candidate goals.
* **Plan to Execute ($\tau_t \to u_t$):** The trajectory planner decodes these leases into smooth, $\mathcal{C}^2$-continuous reference splines $\tau_t$ that respect physical torque and acceleration limits.
* **Execute to World ($u_t \to W_{t+1}$):** Finally, the real-time execution tier filters candidate waypoints through Control Barrier Functions and modulates low-level electrical signals ($u_t$), guaranteeing forward safety invariance while physically transforming the material world ($W_{t+1}$).

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Systems Stress-Tests: Architectural Food for Thought

To transition from conceptual definitions to whole-system architectural reasoning, consider four foundational dilemmas where the cognitive stages and their interfaces are put under stress.

#### Stress-Test 1: The Occluded Hazard Dilemma (Perception & Memory Stages) {.unnumbered}

* **The Scenario:** An autonomous mobile delivery robot navigates a crowded hospital corridor at $1.2\text{ m/s}$. A medical cart momentarily rolls in front of the robot's camera, occluding a descending stairwell that the robot had observed two seconds earlier.

* **The Digital vs. Physical Contrast:** In software simulation, an AI model that processes only the latest camera frame might assume the occluded space is open floor. But in the physical world, gravitational drops and static hazards persist regardless of whether camera photons are currently received.

* **The Systems Dilemma:**
  1. If the robot relies strictly on instantaneous perception ($O_t$), why does the obstacle or drop-off disappear from its decision space the moment line-of-sight is lost?
  2. If a learned world model hallucinates a continuous floor surface behind the cart based on surrounding context, how does the state estimation stage prevent ungrounded hallucinations from driving the robot into danger?
  3. How does tracking positional uncertainty over time determine when the robot must slow down or halt because internal belief has degraded?

* **The Physical AI Insight:** Perception is fundamentally instantaneous and partial ($O_t \neq S_t$). Safe physical agency requires temporal memory to maintain persistent world states across occlusions and sensor dropouts, bounding internal spatial uncertainty before commanding physical motion.

#### Stress-Test 2: The Thermal Throttling Paradox (Reasoning & Planning Stages) {.unnumbered}

* **The Scenario:** A dual-arm robotic manipulator sorts components in a hot factory cell. Under nominal conditions, the high-level semantic reasoning model runs at $2\text{ Hz}$ (emitting intent leases valid for $500\text{ ms}$), while the trajectory planner operates at $50\text{ Hz}$. Due to high ambient temperatures, the main processor throttles its clock speed to prevent overheating.

* **The Digital vs. Physical Contrast:** In cloud computing, a thermal slowdown simply means an API response takes longer. On physical hardware, a compute slowdown means new intent leases arrive after previous leases have already expired.

* **The Systems Dilemma:**
  1. When processor throttling causes neural inference latency to spike from $180\text{ ms}$ to $600\text{ ms}$, why does the active $500\text{ ms}$ intent lease expire before the next command arrives?
  2. If the low-level controller executes an emergency dynamic brake every time a lease expires, why does this start-stop chatter cause destructive torque shock on the joints?
  3. How should the reasoning and planning stages coordinate to adapt trajectory lookahead horizons ($H$) when processor thermal telemetry indicates degraded compute throughput?

* **The Physical AI Insight:** High-level deliberation runs on variable-latency hardware. The interface between semantic reasoning and trajectory planning must use expiring intent leases and multi-step action chunking to buffer the physical robot against computational slowdowns without risking unguided runaway.

#### Stress-Test 3: The Trapped Barrier Dilemma (Planning & Execution Stages) {.unnumbered}

* **The Scenario:** A robotic manipulator reaches into a confined automotive assembly fixture. A high-level trajectory planner proposes a fast path toward the target. At the lowest level, a 1000 Hz real-time safety barrier modifies joint commands to prevent collisions with the fixture walls.

* **The Digital vs. Physical Contrast:** Safety filters in simulation often assume that minimally projecting commands away from obstacles is always safe. In physical kinematics, repeatedly deflecting joint velocities can push an arm into a mechanical singularity where the arm loses the ability to move in certain directions.

* **The Systems Dilemma:**
  1. If the real-time safety enforcer minimally alters joint commands to avoid an obstacle wall, why might these local adjustments inadvertently steer the arm into a kinematic singularity?
  2. In a singular configuration, why do required Cartesian motions demand infinitely large joint speeds ($\dot{\mathbf{q}} \to \infty$), causing joint current limits to trip and halting the robot?
  3. How must the high-level trajectory planner and low-level safety enforcer share kinematic feasibility constraints to prevent local safety filters from causing system deadlocks?

* **The Physical AI Insight:** Real-time safety filters are locally myopic. While kilohertz barrier functions guarantee immediate collision avoidance, the upstream trajectory planner must ensure that candidate paths remain kinematically feasible and far from singular configurations.

#### Stress-Test 4: The Zero-Latency Monolith (Whole-System Integration) {.unnumbered}

* **The Scenario:** Suppose future advancements in computing hardware allow large-scale multimodal foundation models to execute with zero computational latency ($\Delta t = 0\text{ ms}$) and infinite frame rate.

* **The Digital vs. Physical Contrast:** An engineering team argues that with zero-latency neural networks, the five-stage cognitive hierarchy is unnecessary: a single monolithic model can directly map camera pixels to motor voltages in one end-to-end loop.

* **The Systems Dilemma:**
  1. Even if neural computation takes zero time, why do physical constraints—such as camera photon exposure times ($8\text{--}15\text{ ms}$), motor coil inductive rise times ($\tau_e = L/R$), and mechanical inertia ($p=mv$)—still impose hard physical delays?
  2. Why does the requirement for verifiable safety certification permanently mandate a structural separation between a learned proposal policy and a deterministic safety gatekeeper?
  3. Why is decomposing agency into perception, memory, reasoning, planning, and execution a fundamental property of cyber-physical systems rather than an artifact of slow computers?

* **The Physical AI Insight:** The five-stage cognitive lifecycle is governed by the laws of physics and systems verification, not computational speed alone. Even with instantaneous silicon, the boundaries between observation, belief, intent, trajectory, and actuation remain non-negotiable requirements for trustworthy physical intelligence.


## Summary and Forward Handoff

This chapter deconstructed embodied physical agency into five foundational sensory-motor stages: Spatial Perception ($W_t \to O_t$), Temporal Memory ($O_t \to S_t$), Semantic Reasoning ($S_t \to I_t$), Trajectory Planning ($I_t \to \tau_t$), and Real-Time Safety Execution ($\tau_t \to u_t \to W_{t+1}$). We traced the evolutionary transition from classical hand-engineered heuristics to modern Physical AI foundation models, demonstrating how learned representations provide open-world generalizability while formal safety barriers preserve deterministic physical guarantees.

However, a fundamental systems challenge remains unresolved: *How do we physically execute these five cognitive stages across silicon when their computational requirements span four orders of temporal magnitude?* If high-level foundation models require hundreds of milliseconds to deliberate, while motor inverters require microsecond switching updates, how do we prevent slow semantic inference from starving fast physical reflexes?

To answer this question, we turn to **@sec-hierarchy (The Multi-Rate Systems Hierarchy: Decoupling Cognitive Speeds Across Heterogeneous Silicon)**. There, we examine how physical systems decouple execution into three distinct temporal cadences—System 2, System 1.5, and System 1—and formalize the Proposal–Permission boundary across heterogeneous silicon architectures.
